Kansas Public Radio (April 16, 2012) reports that Governor Brownback issued a declaration of disaster emergency early Sunday, April 15, after the April 14 tornadoes.
Scanned proclamation on KDEM's disaster-declarations page (2013 tab), signed August 16, 2013, for storms and flooding from July 22, 2013 and continuing in 60 counties.
Scanned proclamation on KDEM's disaster-declarations page (2014 tab, Baxter Springs tornado), signed April 28, 2014, for the storms of April 27, 2014 and continuing.
Scanned proclamation on KDEM's disaster-declarations page (2015 tab, filed under DR-4230), signed May 28, 2015, for storms and flooding from May 4, 2015 and continuing.
Scanned proclamation on KDEM's disaster-declarations page (2015 tab), signed November 18, 2015, for the winter storm of November 17-18, 2015 in eight northwest Kansas counties.
Scanned proclamation on KDEM's disaster-declarations page (2016 tab), signed September 23, 2016, for heavy rain and flooding from September 2 through 12, 2016 in eleven counties.

Kansas Adjutant General's Department release of September 4, 2018: Governor Colyer has issued a State of Disaster Emergency declaration for flooding over the weekend in five counties. Dated from that release.
Sunflower State Radio (May 9, 2019) reports Governor Kelly issued the declaration that morning for severe storms and flooding; the State Emergency Operations Center opened at about 9 p.m. May 8.
WIBW: the Adjutant General's Office says Governor Kelly verbally declared a State of Disaster Emergency at 9:25 a.m. on December 9, 2021, for elevated wildland fire danger.

Executive Order 01-03, printed in the Kansas Register (Vol. 20, No. 18, May 3, 2001): 'on the twenty-second day of April, 2001, I executed a proclamation declaring a natural disaster' for the severe weather that struck Barton County.

Executive Order 03-09, printed in the Kansas Register (Vol. 22, No. 20, May 15, 2003): 'on the 4th day of May, 2003, I executed a proclamation declaring a natural disaster' for severe weather in several southeast and northeast Kansas counties.
Executive Order 03-10, printed in the Kansas Register (Vol. 22, No. 21, May 22, 2003): 'at 10:00 pm on the eighth day of May, 2003, I declared a state of emergency' for six counties.

Executive Order 03-11, printed in the Kansas Register (Vol. 22, No. 27, July 3, 2003): 'at 10:29 am on the sixteenth day of May, 2003, Lt. Governor John Moore declared a state of disaster emergency' for the severe weather of May 15, 2003.

Kansas Adjutant General's Department releases of December 30, 2006 and January 1, 2007 (archived copies of kansastag.gov): Governor Sebelius declared a state of disaster emergency for 39 counties on December 30, later 44.

Legislation printed in the Kansas Register (Vol. 26, No. 22, May 31, 2007) says Governor Sebelius declared a state of disaster emergency by proclamation on May 4, 2007 for six counties after the May 4 tornado; the Adjutant General's release of May 6 agrees. Her later executive orders (07-07, 07-17) give the date as May 5.

Executive Order 07-18, printed in the Kansas Register (Vol. 27, No. 20, May 15, 2008): 'on the 30th day of June, 2007, I declared a state of emergency' for 17 counties after flooding; the Adjutant General's release of July 1, 2007 says the declaration was signed June 30 for flooding beginning June 29.

Executive Order 07-26, printed in the Kansas Register (Vol. 27, No. 21, May 22, 2008): 'on the 10th day of December, 2007, I declared a state of emergency for the entire 105 counties' for the winter storm of December 10-12, 2007.
Kansas Adjutant General's Department release of June 20, 2008 (archived copy of kansastag.gov): the counties were named in the Governor's original declaration dated May 22, 2008, later amended.

KDEM's ksready.gov page (archived 2009) links 'March Winter Storm State Declaration' as State_Declaration_032709.pdf; the date is taken from that file name. KSCB News (May 21, 2009) confirms Governor Sebelius signed a State of Disaster Emergency declaration for 62 counties for the March storms.

Kansas Adjutant General's Department release of September 9, 2009 (archived copy of kansastag.gov): the six counties were named in a State of Disaster Emergency declaration Governor Parkinson signed July 9, 2009.

Kansas Adjutant General's Department release of November 20, 2009 (archived copy of kansastag.gov): Governor Parkinson signed a State of Disaster Emergency declaration that day for recent winter weather.
KOFO (December 31, 2009): Lt. Governor Troy Findley, on Governor Parkinson's behalf, issued the state disaster declaration for the Christmas blizzard that afternoon.
Kansas Adjutant General's Department release of February 1, 2011 (archived copy of kansastag.gov): the Governor declared a state disaster declaration at 6 a.m. that day for 53 counties.
Kansas Adjutant General's Department release of May 22, 2011 (archived copy of kansastag.gov): Governor Brownback declared a State of Emergency after the storms, naming 16 counties.

Kansas Adjutant General's Department release of Monday, February 25, 2013 (archived copy of kansastag.gov): Governor Brownback signed a State of Disaster Emergency declaration for the entire state on Wednesday (February 20), later amended to include the next storm.
